description: Florida sources for the FactLot Registry collector: the Department of Revenue's statewide NAL (Name-Address-Legal) real property roll files, one per county and year. See docs/registry/data-policy.md and the review record in docs/registry/sources/fl-dor-nal.md.

sources.publisher: Florida Department of Revenue, Property Tax Oversight
sources.license: Public record (ch. 119, F.S.): the data portal states the Department publishes assessment rolls in compliance with chapter 119. The site-wide Conditions of Use page, however, says site material may be downloaded 'for non-commercial use only' and may not be 'copied, reproduced, republished, uploaded, posted, transmitted, or distributed in any way'. Which of the two governs the roll files needs a person's decision
sources.redistribution: Unclear: public record under ch. 119 (and Microdecisions, Inc. v. Skinner, 889 So. 2d 871 (Fla. 2d DCA 2004), held a Florida property appraiser cannot restrict commercial use of its roll data absent a statute), but the site's Conditions of Use forbid redistribution of site material.
sources.notes: Files sit in a SharePoint library (Tax Roll Data Files/NAL/<year>F for final rolls, <year>P for preliminary), one zip per county named '<County> <DOR county number> Final NAL <year>.zip'; all 67 counties are published in the same layout, the six largest are listed here. The library page is script-rendered, so discover reads nothing from it; the file list was taken from the library's REST endpoint (second landing page), which returns JSON only with the header 'Accept: application/json;odata=nometadata' (the collector gets Atom XML and finds no links there). Direct file URLs answer 200 with Last-Modified and ETag; robots.txt restricts only the PowerMapper and SortSite agents. The user's guide (layout and DOR land use codes) is archived with the rolls. verified=false until a person decides whether the Conditions of Use apply to ch. 119 records; the real run used --include-unverified.
